issues.description: The template code defines StockIngredient#retrieveQuantity() but the Stock class (template) calls StockIngredient#getQuantity(). This method-name mismatch causes a compilation error and contradicts the problem requirement to add getters for all private fields. The solution repository uses getQuantity(), so the template is inconsistent with both the problem intent and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient class provide a getQuantity() method (returning the int quantity) to match the calls in Stock and the expected getters in the problem statement. For example, rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() or add a getQuantity() that delegates to retrieveQuantity(). Ensure method name and signature match the solution (public int getQuantity()).

issues.description: The template defines a getter named retrieveQuantity() for StockIngredient, while the rest of the code (Stock methods in the template and the reference solution) expect a standard getQuantity() getter. The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields," implying conventional getter names. This mismatch forces students to reconcile two different method names for the same concept (the ingredient quantity), causes compilation/runtime confusion, and increases extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java (or add a getQuantity() wrapper that returns retrieveQuantity()). This aligns the template with the problem statement's getter convention and with the solution and Stock usage.
